question: Where do the specifications on a switch come from, and what am I looking at?
answer:
Open the scan result and tap the Switches tab (or deep-link to /switch-info/<rack id>). Pick the switch — the card opens on the Specifications tab, under the heading "Hardware".

What you see is the manufacturer's datasheet for the make and model RackTrack read off the chassis in your photo. Nothing is queried from the switch itself — RackTrack does not SSH or SNMP the device for this tab, so it works even when you are not on the switch's network. (It does need to reach the RackTrack server: the app posts the vendor and model to /api/specs, and for a model it has not seen the spec agent may fetch the vendor's datasheet live from the web. Once loaded, the result is cached per rack, vendor and model.)

The rows are a mix of two things:
1. A fixed set of labelled fields when RackTrack has them: Family, SKU, Ports, Port config, Uplinks, Max port speed (Gbps), Switching capacity (Gbps), Forwarding rate (Mpps), Buffer (MB), Latency (ns), MAC table, PoE, PoE budget (W), Power typical (W), Power max (W), Layer, Features, Rack units, Network OS, Status, Typical use.
2. Everything else the spec agent pulled off the vendor's datasheet, keyed by whatever wording the vendor used (these never overwrite a labelled field above) — which is why one switch shows a handful of rows and another shows dozens.

If a field is blank for that model it is left out rather than shown empty. If RackTrack has no vendor/model yet you'll see "Add vendor and model to see specs." Tap "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section to open the vendor's own product page and confirm anything that matters before you order or install.
symptoms: Where do the switch specs come from
Are these specs read from the switch
What is the Hardware section
One switch shows lots of specs and another shows only a few
rootCause: The Specifications tab renders /api/specs, which returns a fixed set of SPEC_KEY_LABELS fields from the spec agent's record plus the agent's free-form extra_specs from the vendor datasheet; empty values are skipped.

question: The switch card says "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo" and there are no specs. What do I do?
answer:
Type the make and model in yourself — the card has a built-in editor and the specs reload as soon as you save.

1. On the Switches tab, expand the device. Its title will be the switch's name if RackTrack has one, otherwise "Unidentified device".
2. Under the heading "Identification" you will see a "Not detected" chip and the line "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo."
3. Tap "Enter make / model" on the right of that heading.
4. Fill in "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. MikroTik) and "Model" (placeholder: e.g. CRS328-24P-4S+RM). Both are required — Save stays greyed out until you have filled in both. Enter saves, Esc cancels.
5. Tap Save. RackTrack re-runs the spec lookup with your values and the chip changes to "Manual entry". The firmware check also re-runs, but only if RackTrack already knows the device's OS version — if it doesn't, add the version with the firmware section's own editor and the check will run then.

Type the model exactly as printed on the chassis, including hyphens and any + signs. If you get it wrong, tap "Edit" and correct it, or tap "Clear" to remove what you entered and go back to whatever the photo produced.

Why it happens: RackTrack reads the make and model off the label in your photo. A device shot at an angle, in shadow, with the label hidden behind cables, or with no printed model on the front will come back blank. (If only one of the two fields came back blank you will see "Vendor not detected" or "Model not detected" instead, and the button reads "Add vendor" / "Add model" — the same editor.)

Not detected chip on the switch card
Unidentified device on the Switches tab
No specs shown for a switch
rootCause: When OCR returns neither manufacturer nor model, identMissing is true and the card surfaces the IdentEditor; saving writes an override and calls loadDetails() again.

question: It got the brand right but the model is missing — "We identified "Cisco" but couldn't read the model. Specs and firmware checks need both."
answer:
Add the missing half by hand. Specs and the firmware check will not run on a brand alone.

1. On the Switches tab, expand the device.
2. Under "Identification" you will see a chip reading either "Model not detected" or "Vendor not detected".
3. Tap the action on the right — it reads "Add model" when the vendor is known, or "Add vendor" when only a model was read.
4. Both boxes ("Make / Vendor" and "Model") appear, prefilled with whatever was detected. Fill in the blank one and leave the other as it is. Save stays greyed out until both boxes have text, then tap Save (or press Enter).

Saving re-runs the lookup immediately — the Specifications tab switches from "Add vendor and model to see specs." to the real spec table, and the firmware check runs too (if an OS version is known). You do not need to close and reopen the card.

Afterwards the chip reads "Manual entry" and the link becomes "Edit", so you can correct the values later or clear them to fall back on what the scan read.

This half-detected case is common: the brand name is usually a big silkscreen logo that survives a bad photo, while the model number is small printed text on a sticker. If you can, get closer to the label and re-shoot the rack; otherwise just type the model in.

question: I typed in the make and model on the Switches tab, but my colleague still sees "Unidentified device" — and it vanished when I used a different phone.
answer:
That is expected. A make/model you type on the Switches tab is saved only in the browser or app you typed it in. It is not sent to the server, so it does not travel to your teammates, to another phone, or to a browser where you cleared site data.

What it does do: it sticks on that device for you across reloads. The saved value is keyed to the device's serial number, MAC address or U position — deliberately not to the make/model you can change — so it survives a re-scan that reads different text off the label. (If the device has no serial, MAC or position at all, the value is pinned to the detected device name instead, and a re-scan that names it differently will lose it.)

If the whole team needs the corrected identity:
- Correct the device on the scan result itself instead. Open the device from the Device list and answer "No" to "Detected as <type> — right?" for the device type; that correction is posted to the server and merged into the scan, so your organisation sees it.
- For the make and model specifically there is no shared correction: everyone who needs the specs has to type it once on their own device, or you re-shoot the rack with the label readable so the photo picks it up for everyone.

To remove your typed value, expand the device, tap "Edit" under Identification, and tap "Clear". (Before you have entered anything, that button reads "Enter make / model", "Add model" or "Add vendor" instead of "Edit".)
symptoms: My make/model correction isn't visible to my team
Manual entry disappeared on another device
Typed model didn't save for everyone
Manual entry chip only shows for me
rootCause: saveOverride writes to localStorage under racktrack:<field>:<rackId>::<stableId>; there is no server round-trip, so the override is per browser profile.

question: [Internal] How does the OCR model auto-correction work, and does the UI tell the user it happened?
answer:
Internal only — do not describe this mechanism to customers beyond "RackTrack may correct a misread model number".

POST /api/specs and POST /api/firmware both take an optional `fromOcr` flag (server/app.js:7009 and 7190).

Who sets it:
- client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:309 — direct fetches set it to `!!sw._fromOcr && !modelIsUserSupplied`, i.e. OCR-derived AND the user has not manually overridden the model.
- client/src/utils/scanPrefetch.js:172 and :184 — the background prefetcher always sends `fromOcr: true` for every OCR device it walks. So a prefetched, client-cached spec/firmware result may already contain a substitution even for a device the technician later edits.

When fromOcr is true, resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection (server/app.js:7071-7090) runs:
1. A DB-only probe (`--no-live`) on "<vendor> <model>". On a hit it returns with matchedFrom/matchedTo null.
2. Otherwise it takes probe.response.suggestions and scores each against the queried model with _modelSimilarity (server/app.js:7032-7050) = 0.6 * (shared-prefix chars / shorter string length) + 0.4 * (in-order common chars / longer string length), alphanumeric-normalised and case-insensitive. _bestSuggestion (7052-7065) returns the top scorer only if its score is >= 0.5. If that suggestion differs from the query, it retries live with "<vendor> <suggestion>"; a successful retry returns matchedFrom = original model, matchedTo = suggestion.
3. If the retry fails or no suggestion qualifies, it falls back to a live lookup of the original query and reports no substitution.

When a substitution happened the response carries matchedFrom (what OCR read) and matchedTo (what was actually looked up) — /api/specs at 7021-7024, /api/firmware at 7211-7214. A grep of client/src shows nothing reads either field, so the swap is invisible in the UI. That is the root cause of "the specs are for a different model" tickets.

/api/firmware runs the same probe purely for its matchedTo (the probe's spec result is discarded) and sets firmwareModel = matchedTo || model before calling the agent's --firmware mode (7199-7207), so a bad substitution also skews the firmware verdict. Note the response's `model` field still echoes the model the client sent, not matchedTo.
symptoms: User reports specs for a sibling model
matchedFrom / matchedTo in the API response
Why did the lookup use a different model number
rootCause: resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection substitutes a similar model above a 0.5 similarity threshold and the client never renders matchedFrom/matchedTo, so the swap is invisible.

question: How does RackTrack work out the make and model from a photo — and what can I do to help it?
answer:
It reads the printed label on the front of each device. For the devices worth OCRing — switches, servers, routers, firewalls, aggregation/core gear, and anything the scan couldn't classify — RackTrack crops that device out of your rack photo, enlarges the crop if it's less than about 120 pixels tall, and runs text recognition on it three times (plain, contrast-boosted and sharpened) so faint text on dark plastic still comes out. Patch panels, PDUs, UPS units and blank panels are deliberately skipped: they rarely carry model text and OCRing them just adds noise.

It then works through the recognised text in this order:

1. Model-number patterns first. If the text contains something shaped like a known SKU — for example WS-C…/C9300-48P (Cisco), TL-SG… (TP-Link), DGS-/DXS- (D-Link), EX/QFX/MX/SRX (Juniper), CRS/CCR/CSS/RB (MikroTik), USW-/UDM-/ES- (Ubiquiti UniFi and EdgeSwitch), GS/JGS/XS (NETGEAR) and others — that both gives the model and fixes the brand.
2. If no model pattern matches, it looks for a manufacturer name from RackTrack's vendor list.
3. If that fails, it looks for brand words like Catalyst, Nexus, Meraki, JetStream, Omada, ProCurve, PowerEdge, ProSafe, UniFi, RouterOS, FortiGate and DiskStation, and tolerates common misreads (Csco, Unfi, Mikrorik) via a fuzzy match.

What helps, in order of impact:
- Shoot the rack straight on, not from the side — the label has to be square to the lens.
- Get light on the front panel; the label is usually small dark text.
- Move cables off the label if you can.
- Fill the frame with the rack so each device gets more pixels.

If it still misses, open the device on the Switches tab and use the "Identification" section — "Enter make / model" — to type them in. Saving clears the cached results and re-runs the specs and firmware lookups straight away. (Both fields are needed: with only a vendor, specs and firmware checks can't run.)
symptoms: How does it know the brand of my switch
Where does the make and model come from
Why did it not read my switch label
How do I take a photo it can read
rootCause: pipeline/ocr_devices.py crops each detected device, upscales to ~120px tall, runs three EasyOCR passes and parses make/model with per-vendor regexes, then the vendor sheet, then fuzzy brand keywords.

question: The Switches tab just says "Scanning…" / "Run a rack scan to detect switches." and never fills in.
answer:
Reading the chassis labels (per-device OCR) is a separate, slower step that the server kicks off in the background once your scan finishes — on CPU it takes roughly 1-2 minutes for a full rack. Until it writes its result, the Switches tab has nothing to list and shows the misleading "Scanning…" empty state.

What to do:
1. Wait a minute or two, then leave the Switches tab and come back. The tab only checks once, when it opens — it does not keep retrying — so re-opening it (or reloading the page) is what triggers a fresh check.
2. If it is still empty after several minutes, confirm the scan actually found devices: the rack Overview should show a unit map with devices in it. No detected devices means there is nothing to read labels from.
3. If devices were detected but no switch appears, the rack may contain no device classified as a switch. This tab lists switches only — routers and patch panels are deliberately excluded even when detected.

Older scans taken before label-reading existed will also stay empty; re-scan the rack to get identification for it.

Run a rack scan to detect switches
Switch Information never loads
Switches tab empty after a scan
rootCause: GET /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices returns 404 until ocr_devices.json exists; the prefetcher gives up after 8 consecutive 404s until the page is reloaded, and the empty state renders when the switch list is empty.

question: [Internal] A rack keeps showing the same wrong make/model after re-processing. How is device identification re-run?
answer:
Internal only.

Per-device label OCR is written once per rack to outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json. scheduleOcrDevices() (server/app.js:1577) is a fire-and-forget spawn of `python -m pipeline.ocr_devices <rackId> --json` and returns immediately if that file already exists, or if device_unit_map.json is missing (server/app.js:1583). It is only called from scheduleCanonicalRefresh() (server/app.js:1478), so a canonical refresh, a Netdisco resync, or re-opening the rack all keep serving the original identification.

To force a re-identification: POST /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices (server/app.js:7356). It runs pipeline.ocr_devices synchronously with a 5-minute timeout (OCR_DEVICES_TIMEOUT_MS, server/app.js:7355; EasyOCR on CPU is the slow path, 1-2 min for a full rack), 404s if outputs/<rackId> does not exist, 504s on timeout, and returns the parsed JSON. pipeline/ocr_devices.py always rewrites outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json (line 588), so the cached result is overwritten. GET on the same path only reads that cached file (404 if OCR has never run).

Important caveat: only the background run re-syncs downstream — after a successful spawn, scheduleOcrDevices rewrites the canonical scan result and reschedules the Netdisco sync (server/app.js:1600-1608). The POST endpoint does NOT do this. After forcing a re-run via POST you must also trigger a canonical refresh / CMDB rebuild, or downstream consumers (synth.py, Netdisco, CMDB) keep serving the old synthesized make/model.

Customer-facing wording: tell the user to re-scan the rack (new rack id, therefore a fresh OCR run). Do not give customers the endpoint.
symptoms: Same wrong model after reprocessing a rack
ocr_devices.json not regenerated
How to force re-identification
rootCause: scheduleOcrDevices short-circuits when outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json exists, so identification is computed exactly once per rack id.

question: How do I look up the datasheet for a device that isn't in a scan?
answer:
Use the Specifications screen at /specifications — it is a standalone lookup and is not linked from the sidebar or bottom nav today, so navigate to the URL directly (you must be signed in). On a desktop or tablet the top bar then reads "Specifications / Vendor & model lookup"; the page heading is "Find datasheet specs for a device."

1. Type the maker into "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. Cisco, Juniper, Aruba). Up to six matching vendor suggestions appear as you type — tap one to fill the box.
2. Type the model into "Model" (placeholder: e.g. C9300-48P, EX4400-24T).
3. Tap "Get specifications". The button reads "Searching…" while it works. Leaving either box empty gives "Both vendor and model are required."

You get a summary card with the vendor and model, a line reading "We pulled N specs from the vendor's product page — here are the most useful ones at a glance", and up to five headline rows picked from Ports, Throughput, Layer, Form factor, Power, PoE, Uplinks, MAC table and Stacking. If the product page is found but no spec table can be extracted, it says so instead.

Underneath:
- "Open product page ↗" — opens the vendor's own page in a new tab (shown only when a product URL was found).
- "Show all specs (N)" — expands the full spec table; it then reads "Hide all specs".

This screen is a pure lookup: it does not touch your rack, your scans or your CMDB, and nothing you type here is saved to a scan.

question: The vendor box doesn't suggest my manufacturer, or it says "Vendor list unavailable". Can I still search?
answer:
Yes — type the vendor name in anyway and tap "Get specifications". The suggestion list is only a convenience; the lookup itself does not require the name to be on it.

Things to know about that list:
- It comes from RackTrack's vendor sheet on the server, loaded once when the screen opens.
- It only shows suggestions once you start typing, and never more than six at a time — keep typing to narrow it down.
- If the server could not supply it you get "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the box. The search still works.

You do always need both fields filled in — leaving "Make / Vendor" or "Model" empty gives "Both vendor and model are required."

If the lookup then comes back with no match, the vendor spelling is usually not the problem — re-check the Model field instead and enter the exact SKU as printed on the device, hyphens included (e.g. C9300-48P). Very short or generic model strings are the most common cause of a miss; if it still misses, confirm the full part number on the maker's own site.
symptoms: My vendor isn't in the dropdown
Vendor list unavailable
No suggestions when typing a vendor
Only six vendor suggestions
rootCause: The type-ahead is populated from GET /api/specs/vendors (the vendor Excel sheet) and sliced to 6; POST /api/specs passes the typed vendor string straight through without validating it against that list.

question: The Specifications screen shows "Both vendor and model are required." or an error about the backend / port 3001.
answer:
Three different messages, three different causes:

"Both vendor and model are required." — you left one of the two boxes empty. Fill in both Make / Vendor and Model, then tap "Get specifications" again. Nothing was sent to the server.

"Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …). Is the server running?" — the request reached something, but it did not answer with a result. Usually a server-side problem, not yours.

"Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?" — the request never completed at all: no signal, no network, a VPN that just dropped, or RackTrack's server unreachable from where you are standing.

For the last two: check you have a working data or Wi-Fi connection, then retry once. If it keeps failing while the rest of the app works, report it to your administrator with the exact message and the make/model you typed — it is a server-side fault, not something you can fix on the phone.

Backend returned a non-JSON response

rootCause: SpecificationsPage validates both fields client-side, then distinguishes an unparsable response body from a thrown fetch error and shows a different banner for each.

question: It says "We found the product page but couldn't extract a spec table" — where are the specs?
answer:
RackTrack located the manufacturer's page for your model but could not turn it into a table — some vendors publish specs as a PDF, an image, or behind a tab that has to be clicked. The lookup itself succeeded; the extractor just returned zero fields.

Use the link instead:
- On the Specifications screen, tap "Open product page ↗" in the summary card and read the specs on the vendor's own page.
- If the lookup failed outright but a candidate page was still found, you get "Found a candidate page but couldn't extract specs:" followed by the URL — tap it.
- On a switch card's Specifications/Hardware tab, the same link is "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section. With zero specs the table below it will be empty — that is expected, not a loading state.

If no link appears either, the vendor page had no datasheet or image URL to fall back on; search the vendor's site for the model directly.

There is nothing to retry here — re-running the same vendor/model gives the same result. A different model from the same vendor will often extract fine. If you need the numbers recorded against the rack, note them from the vendor page.

(Evidence line fix: the server-side `return { ok: true, ..., productUrl: rec.datasheet_url || rec.image_url || null, ... }` is at server/app.js:7141-7147 inside specPayloadFromAgent, declared at 7110 — not 7087-7093.)

question: What is the "Login portal" / "Vendor site" chip next to the switch name?
answer:
It is a shortcut to the manufacturer's own website for the brand RackTrack identified. It appears on the small grey line directly beneath the device name on the switch card, alongside the U position and IP address.

- "Login portal" means RackTrack has that maker's actual customer/support sign-in page on file — tap it to sign in to the vendor and look up entitlement, downloads or case history. For brands that were absorbed by another company, the link goes to the parent brand's portal (for example an Aerohive switch opens the Extreme Networks sign-in).
- "Vendor site" means RackTrack only has a general support or landing page for that maker.
- No chip at all means the make is blank, or the make RackTrack read didn't match anything in its vendor list — usually an unusual spelling.

To make the chip appear when the make is missing or misread:
1. Tap the switch card to expand it.
2. Under "Identification", tap "Enter make / model" (or "Add vendor" / "Edit").
3. Fill in BOTH "Make / Vendor" and "Model" — Save stays greyed out until both boxes have text.
4. Tap Save. The card re-checks specs and firmware, and the chip appears if the make matches a known vendor.

The chip opens in your phone's browser, in a new tab, not inside RackTrack. RackTrack does not have your vendor account — you sign in with your own company's credentials on the vendor's site. Tapping the chip does not expand or collapse the switch card.
symptoms: What is the Login portal link
Vendor site chip on the switch card
No vendor link shown for my switch
Where do I sign in to the manufacturer
rootCause: SwitchCard calls findVendorLogin(effectiveMake) against a generated vendor→portal map; source 'login' renders the "Login portal" chip, 'fallback' renders "Vendor site", null renders nothing.
